read_me: Every w_m is either null ('needs field calibration') or carries a key into 'sources'.
Null is the honest default. The primary path is a field calibration table (AMDR/ADD or Rd trial: W = factor x range) supplied with --calibration; see sweep_width.py.
Values in 'leads' were seen only in secondary or tertiary summaries. The code never reads them; they say where to look when calibrating.

ground_searcher.description: single ground searcher walking a track (grid/line member)

hasty_team.description: hasty team on trails and likely spots

target.responsive_adult: adult able to respond to calls / move toward searchers
target.unresponsive_adult: adult who does not respond (unconscious, deceased, hiding); detection-experiment objects (stationary, silent) belong here
target.clothing_clue: clue-sized object (garment, pack, item of clothing)

vegetation.open: no canopy or understorey blocking view (field, meadow, open tundra, bare ground)
vegetation.deciduous_leaf_off: deciduous forest in leaf-off season (e.g. winter hardwood)
vegetation.forest_moderate: forest or scrub with moderate canopy/understorey
vegetation.forest_dense: dense forest / thick understorey (e.g. temperate rainforest)

visibility.high: high-visibility object (bright clothing, strong contrast) - Koester et al. 2014 class
visibility.medium: medium-visibility object - Koester et al. 2014 class
visibility.low: low-visibility object (dark/camouflage clothing, low contrast) - Koester et al. 2014 class

koester2004.citation: Koester R.J., Cooper D.C., Frost J.R., Robe R.Q. (30 Dec 2004). Sweep Width Estimation for Ground Search and Rescue. Potomac Management Group, prepared for the U.S. Coast Guard / National SAR Committee. DTIC accession ADA511593.
koester2004.verification: secondary: the extreme values (142 m, 17 m) are quoted from the report's summary as reproduced by the dbS Productions newsletter and the DTIC record, retrieved via web search on 2026-10-16. The primary PDF could not be opened from this session (egress proxy 403). Check against the report's results tables before operational use.
koester2004.note: The task brief cited DTIC ADA511658; the accession found for this title is ADA511593. ADA511658 was not confirmed.

koester2014.citation: Koester R.J., Chiacchia K.B., Twardy C.R., Cooper D.C., Frost J.R., Robe R.Q. (2014). Use of the visual range of detection to estimate effective sweep width for land search and rescue based on 10 detection experiments in North America. Wilderness & Environmental Medicine 25(2):132-142. doi:10.1016/j.wem.2013.09.016
koester2014.verification: abstract: factors 1.8 / 1.6 / 1.1 x Rd are stated in the abstract (several independent abstract listings agree, retrieved via web search 2026-10-16). The abstract itself says more experiments are needed for medium- and low-visibility objects and the dry-domain ecoregion.

chiacchia2015.citation: Chiacchia K.B., Houlahan H.E., Hostetter R.S. (2015). Deriving effective sweep width for air-scent dog teams. Wilderness & Environmental Medicine 26(2):142-149. doi:10.1016/j.wem.2014.10.004
chiacchia2015.verification: not verified: headline W value not retrieved from the paper; see leads.

chiacchia2023.citation: Chiacchia K.B., Houlahan H.E. (January 2023). Field POD data fitted to the exponential and inverse-cube detection models to derive effective sweep width for air-scent dog teams and human searchers. Journal of Search and Rescue (January 2023 issue).
chiacchia2023.verification: method only: abstract-level summary (least-squares fits of field POD, R^2 > 0.8, detector-agnostic). No W values retrieved; exact title not confirmed.

dumencic2025.citation: Dumencic S., Lanca L., Jakac K., Ivic S. (2025). Experimental validation of UAV search and detection system in real wilderness environment. Drones 9(7):473; arXiv:2502.17372.
dumencic2025.verification: not verified: trial (Mediterranean karst, 78 volunteers, YOLO detector, HEDAC control) confirmed; no POD or sweep-width numbers retrieved.

hakimipanah2025.citation: Hakimipanah M., Pelot R., Goerlandt F. (2025). Assessing drone performance and probability of detection for search and rescue operation in Northern Canada. Proceedings of ISCRAM, vol. 22 (2025-07-08).
hakimipanah2025.verification: not verified: no numbers retrieved. Note its PoD model is a fuzzy-logic system from expert-elicited factors, not a field lateral-range experiment; do not treat its outputs as measured sweep widths.

gedi_l2b.citation: GEDI L2B Canopy Cover and Vertical Profile Metrics, product data dictionary (LP DAAC). 'cover': total canopy cover, fraction 0-1, the share of ground hidden by the vertical projection of canopy material; 'pgap_theta': total gap probability at view zenith theta.
gedi_l2b.verification: data dictionary definitions retrieved via web search 2026-10-16.

range_to_sweep_width.description: W = factor x Rd, Rd the field-measured visual range of detection (an AMDR/ADD-style trial), by search-object visibility class.

leads.about: ground searcher, Virginia winter hardwood, blue-clad human
leads.seen_in: web-search summary of the DTIC record only; visibility class not stated
tertiary: cited by Hassler et al. 2024, Wildlife Society Bulletin, doi:10.1002/wsb.1558

leads.attributed_to: a Chiacchia & Houlahan study (which one not confirmed)

entries.note: Highest value in the 2004 experiments: high-visibility adult, winter (leaf-off) deciduous forest, Virginia. Detection-experiment object (stationary, silent) mapped to unresponsive_adult; that mapping is this module's interpretation.
Lowest value in the 2004 experiments: low-visibility adult, dense marine forest, western Washington. Same object mapping as above.
